name: University Valley, Quartermain Mountains, McMurdo Dry Valleys (Antarctica)
research_extent: Valley floor around the met/ground-temperature station cluster (1661-1697 m a.s.l.); polygon outline NOT obtained
boundary_basis: Marinova 2022 p.145 (valley 77°52'S 160°45'E, ~1700 m) and p.146 (stations 77°51.729'S 160°42.606'E, 1661-1697 m); boundary = station cluster, not a surveyed polygon
available_data: Air T/RH 1.2 m, wind 1.08 m, ground T at surface/10/42/49 cm, 2009-12 to 2013-01 (Marinova Table II p.153); ice-table depth 10-60 cm (Heldmann 2013 abstract)
testable_physical_processes: Dry cover over ice-cemented ground: how ice-table depth, cover and seasonal heating couple; sublimation/vapour exchange; whether a thermal signal is separable from cover
main_environment_differences: Latitude 77.9°S vs 52.75°N; MAAT -23.4 °C measured vs Mars MCS 03/15 LTST surface medians (not annual mean); atmosphere, pressure, dust, insolation all differ; ice in dry soil at 42 cm vs MS-02 ice depth unknown
disposition_reason: Only candidate with a measured multi-depth temperature series that brackets an ice table and a published energy-balance model; directly addresses 'cover + season + ice' hypotheses H1/H2
cannot_extrapolate: Not a proof that MS-02 has ice; no extrapolation of 42 cm ice-table depth, temperatures or water activity to MS-02
next_verification_step: Obtain Table II/Fig. 6 series from the paper/supplement; get soil density and heat capacity (only conductivity and diffusivity were read, so thermal inertia is not derived); find wind-speed values; test what TES-scale (3 km) thermal inertia could/couldn't see for a 42 cm ice table

name: Middle Beacon Valley, Quartermain Mountains (Antarctica)
research_extent: Not defined: coordinates not extracted; only valley name and Heldmann 2013 / Bannister 2007 abstracts read
boundary_basis: Heldmann 2013 abstract (middle Beacon Valley massive ground ice); Kowalewski 2006 abstract (central Beacon Valley); McKay 2009 abstract; Bannister 2007 abstract (1.3 km transect)
available_data: Heldmann 2013 (ice 10-60 cm, abstract); Kowalewski 2006 (ice under 40-80 cm sublimation till; net loss ~0.017 mm over 18 Nov-29 Dec 2004, HOBO loggers; abstract); McKay 2009 (snow recurrence >10 yr implied on Beacon floor; abstract); Bannister 2007 undergraduate thesis (buried massive ice reported >100 m deep)
testable_physical_processes: Massive buried ice beneath thin dry cover; sublimation-rate and humidity/temperature sensitivity of buried ice; snow recurrence control on ice depth; geophysical detection of massive vs cemented ice
main_environment_differences: Same latitude/climate mismatch as E01; ice type differs (massive ice vs ice-cemented); all evidence is abstract-level; site coordinates still not found; Heldmann (10-60 cm) and Kowalewski (40-80 cm) depth ranges differ by site/definition and were not reconciled
disposition_reason: Now has two peer-reviewed abstracts with numbers (sublimation, till depth) and a snow-recurrence link, but no coordinates, no temperature tables, and no full text read
cannot_extrapolate: Sublimation of 0.017 mm over 6 weeks and 40-80 cm till depth are Beacon Valley values; Bannister 100 m depth is not peer-reviewed and not cross-checked
next_verification_step: Read Kowalewski 2006 and McKay 2009 full text for site coordinates and instrument/depth details; read Marchant & Head 2007 (not yet read)

name: Adventdalen, central Spitsbergen, Svalbard (Norway)
research_extent: Valley floor/terraces of Adventdalen (~40 km long, up to ~3 km wide); point anchor = ADE terrace site; polygon troughs surveyed by WISDOM team
boundary_basis: Hauber 2011 p.113 (valley dimensions, no coordinates); Rotem 2023 (ADE 78.1722°N 16.0613°E, 23 m a.s.l.; valley centre 78.110°N 16.180°E)
available_data: Svalbard Airport climate 1912-1993 (Hauber Table 1 p.114); Adventdalen 'Polygons' MAAT -5.8 °C (Rotem 2023); HRSC-AX DEMs 0.5-1 m (Hauber pp.112-113); WISDOM GPR Mar 2022 (Brighi 2025); loess OSL record (Rasmussen 2023); PANGAEA polygon geomorphometry dataset (lead, not read)
testable_physical_processes: Ice-wedge polygons and mantled ground ice; aeolian silt cover (loess) building syngenetic permafrost; radar detection of ice beneath an active layer; polygon geometry vs Mars (Hauber)
main_environment_differences: Latitude 78°N; thicker, wetter, vegetated-valley setting not described in what I read; MAAT -5.8 °C; saline/epigenetic permafrost part (Rotem); polygons 10-20 m vs Mars example 5-10 m (Hauber Fig 4)
disposition_reason: Best-documented case for the 'mantle + wind + ice detection' questions (H2, H3): measured loess accumulation rate, polygon-trough GPR ice reflector, and a published Mars mid-latitude landform comparison
cannot_extrapolate: Svalbard loess accumulation rates and active-layer depth cannot be transferred to Mars dust deposition or MS-02 cover thickness; GPR ε values are for Earth materials
next_verification_step: Download polygon dataset (PANGAEA 10.1594/PANGAEA.921087 lead) and read Hauber Section 3 for polygon statistics; collect active-layer and borehole series from public permafrost networks (not yet searched)

name: Haughton River Valley, Haughton impact structure, Devon Island, Nunavut (Canada)
research_extent: Nine LiDAR grids (0.1-0.5 m/px) within ~3.9 km N-S x ~4.0 km E-W (this-study calc from Table 3.1 UTM 16N); valley ~1.5 km wide, elevation 75-151 m a.s.l.
boundary_basis: Andres 2020 Table 3.1 (UTM 16N grids converted to 75.359-75.394°N, 89.510-89.655°W) and Fig 1.8 p.20 (75.37, -89.53); the structure centre 75°22'N 89°41'W (p.6) is a different anchor ~4.3 km away
available_data: MAAT ~-16 °C Devon / ~-15 °C valley (cited, Andres p.1,6); LiDAR 2016 (36 DEMs, 9 analysed); thaw depth 0.52-0.67 m (2019, Andres pp.102-106); polygon/stripe diameters 5-31 m (pp.114-115); no Haughton GPR; no Haughton ground-ice quantity
testable_physical_processes: Polar-desert patterned-ground geometry (polygons, stripes, stone circles) and active-layer thaw depth at LiDAR scale; Arcadia-class comparison only via Hibbard thesis (abstract)
main_environment_differences: Impact structure setting at 75°N, MAAT ~-15 to -16 °C; ground-ice content (10-20%) is a Canadian High Arctic generality, not Haughton data; Axel Heiberg GPR/ice-wedge volume is a different site; author states nine grids in a very small locale may not generalise (p.115)
disposition_reason: Measured thaw depth and polygon geometry exist, but no Haughton ground-ice quantity, ground-temperature series, GPR or Mars-point comparison were found in the text read
cannot_extrapolate: Thaw depth (0.52-0.67 m) is a July 2019 snapshot; the 10-20% ice content must not be applied to Haughton or MS-02
next_verification_step: Find Haughton ground-temperature/borehole or GPR data (not found in searches so far); read Hibbard thesis body to see whether Devon/Haughton is among its Arctic sites
